title: Chicken Breast, Stewed, Skin Not Eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed chicken breast without skin is a lean source of protein obtained by slowly simmering the meat in a small amount of liquid. The cooking method retains most nutrients, yields tender meat, and is easy to digest.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast contains very little fat, especially when the skin is removed.
Stewing helps preserve moisture and flavor, making the meat softer than when it is fried.
Chicken is one of the most affordable complete protein sources worldwide.
Different cuisines use various herbs, spices, and vegetables for stewing, creating diverse flavor profiles.
Stewed chicken breast is a staple in diet plans and athletic nutrition.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 31 g of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Without skin, fat content is under 2 g per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken breast supplies niacin (B3), vitamin B6, and small amounts of B12, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: The soft texture of stewed meat makes it gentle on the stomach.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: A small number of people can experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding salt or pre‑made sauces can raise sodium levels, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Vitamin loss with prolonged cooking
items.content: Some water‑soluble vitamins, such as B6, may degrade during long stewing periods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed chicken breast can be sliced and served as a main dish, added to salads, soups, stews, pasta, or used in sandwiches. It can also be diced and frozen for quick future meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the cooked meat to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.
